title: Headless: Serve Content to Any Front End | Orchard Core
description:
A front end that lives in its own application needs three things from its content back end: a way to read the content, permission from the browser to call it, and a way to identify the caller.

Orchard Core provides them with the GraphQL module for queries, the CORS Configuration module for cross-origin policies, and the OpenID Connect Authorization Server and Token Validation features for access tokens.

In this video:
• What headless means, and the three questions it raises
• Reading content with GraphQL, and allowing the Execute GraphQL permission
• Letting a front end on another origin call Orchard Core with a CORS policy
• Registering a public client in OpenID Connect, and validating its tokens
• Applying the same setup on another site with a recipe
